/itineraryStops/0/whyOnRoute.source_en: **Small-group cruise pickup** at the Jeju International Passenger Terminal arrival hall gives the guide time to confirm guest names, walking comfort, photo priorities, and any key requests before departure. The smaller vehicle and group size make boarding simpler than a large coach and give the route more flexibility if ship clearance or weather changes. The 30-minute post-clearance buffer is kept so the group can start calmly without putting the ship-return timing at risk.

/itineraryStops/0/description.source_en:
Your driver and English-speaking guide meet your party at the **Jeju International Passenger Terminal** (제주항 국제여객터미널, address: 191 Imhang-ro, Jeju-si — UN/LOCODE **KRCHA**), the northern coast cruise port that opened in **2015** to receive international cruise vessels. 

The terminal has two berths — the **Main Berth (360 m, 12 m water depth, 140,000-ton capacity)** and an **Emergency Berth (306 m, 11.5 m water depth, 85,000-ton capacity)** — handling **one cruise ship at a time**. Pickup is timed for **30 minutes after your ship's posted clearance**, absorbing immigration variance during multi-ship arrivals. 

The driver carries an English/Korean name placard, a printed itinerary card (with all stop times and Korean-script addresses for emergency taxi use), and the operator's 24/7 contact number. Vehicle is parked in the **100-bus parking capacity lot** adjacent to the arrival hall. 

Before boarding, the guide reviews the day's flow, all-aboard time, weather, and any port-day adjustments. If your guests need currency exchange (Jeju Bank), a SIM/Wi-Fi rental, or use of the multilingual tourist information center, the guide accompanies — these are all on-site within the terminal. 

Per **South Korea's Ministry of Culture, Sports & Tourism**, **810,000 cruise tourists arrived on 414 ships in 2024** — nearly tripling the prior year — so terminal congestion is realistic on multi-ship days.

/itineraryStops/1/timeUsed/2.source_en: Summit views + crater rim photos — ~20 min

/itineraryStops/1/timeUsed/4.source_en: Optional haenyeo viewing at base (14:00 show; may be canceled in bad weather) — ~10 min

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/0.source_en: **Triple UNESCO**: World Heritage 2007-07-02 + Biosphere Reserve 2002 + Global Geopark 2010-10

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/1.source_en: **5,000 years old** — Surtseyan-type hydrovolcanic eruption, magma-meets-seawater steam-explosive birth
/itineraryStops/1/highlights/1.tm: **5.000 Jahre alt** — hydrovulkanischer Ausbruch vom Surtseyanischen Typ, dampfexplosive Entstehung, als Magma auf Meerwasser traf

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/2.source_en: Crater **600 m wide × 90 m deep**, ringed by **99 jagged rim rocks** (the 'stone crown')
/itineraryStops/1/highlights/2.tm: Krater **600 m breit × 90 m tief**, umringt von **99 zackigen Felsen am Kraterrand** (die „Steinkrone“)

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/3.source_en: **182 m above sea level** — 0.8 km / ~140 m gain, 60-min round trip on stone-step trail
/itineraryStops/1/highlights/3.tm: **182 m über dem Meeresspiegel** — 0,8 km / ~140 m Anstieg, 60 Min. Hin- und Rückweg auf einem Pfad mit Steinstufen

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/4.source_en: **18 Imperial Japanese WWII caves** at base — 1945 kamikaze suicide-boat shelters
/itineraryStops/1/highlights/4.tm: **18 kaiserlich-japanische Höhlen aus dem 2. Weltkrieg** am Fuß — 1945 Unterstände für Kamikaze-Selbstmordboote

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/5.source_en: **Haenyeo demonstration once daily at 14:00 (subject to bad-weather cancellation)** at the seaside cove — UNESCO Intangible 2016
/itineraryStops/1/highlights/5.tm: **Haenyeo-Vorführung einmal täglich um 14:00 Uhr (Ausfall bei schlechtem Wetter möglich)** in der Bucht am Meer — immaterielles UNESCO-Erbe 2016

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/6.source_en: **Admission updated April 2025**: Adult ₩5,000 / Youth ₩2,500 / FREE under 7 + over 65
/itineraryStops/1/highlights/6.tm: **Eintritt aktualisiert im April 2025**: Erwachsene ₩5.000 / Jugendliche ₩2.500 / KOSTENLOS unter 7 + über 65

/itineraryStops/1/highlights/8.source_en: **Closes for first Monday of each month** (occasional rest day)

/itineraryStops/1/smartNotes/tip.source_en: All stairs but well-maintained — manageable in casual clothes; family-friendly with rest stops; sunrise visits popular but crowds gather pre-dawn
/itineraryStops/1/smartNotes/tip.tm: Alles Treppen, aber gut instand gehalten — in Alltagskleidung machbar; familienfreundlich mit Rastmöglichkeiten; Besuche zum Sonnenaufgang sind beliebt, doch die Menge sammelt sich schon vor der Dämmerung

/itineraryStops/1/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Café (Fritz Coffee 1.3km away has best exterior views of the peak); ferry to Udo Island from Seongsan Port (1.5km/15 min walk)
/itineraryStops/1/smartNotes/facilities.tm: Café (Fritz Coffee, 1,3 km entfernt, bietet die besten Außenansichten des Gipfels); Fähre zur Insel Udo ab dem Hafen Seongsan (1,5 km / 15 Min. zu Fuß)

/itineraryStops/1/whyOnRoute.source_en: **⟦G0⟧ is the main natural highlight of the east route.** The small-group format gives guests more time for photos, questions, and pace adjustments on the crater trail. The guide can explain the 5,000-year-old volcanic formation, the sea views, and the haenyeo culture around the base without rushing the group. If conditions or guest mobility make the full climb unsuitable, the visit can still work well from the lower viewing areas.

/itineraryStops/1/convenience/restroom.tm: Am Eingang und am Fuß vorhanden
